record.field: Tool to sort the marketing campaign activities.

# Campaign Activities Sorter
This tool recomputes the `coordinates` of every activity in a campaign so the workflow displays correctly in the UI.
Run it after each create that adds activities, and after any change to a `parent_id` or `triggering_activity_id` - not once at the end. A new activity has no position until this runs, so everything added since the last sort sits at the origin, stacked on top of what was already there, while the user watches the canvas.
Never set `coordinates` yourself. This tool is the only thing that sets them, and it takes no spacing, offset, direction or arrangement parameters - it recomputes the entire layout in one pass or not at all.
So when a user asks for manual positioning - more space between steps, a specific arrangement, moving one step - tell them that isn't available, offer to re-run the automatic layout instead, and ask before running it. Do not run it uninvited in response to a layout request, and do not reorder or restructure activities as a substitute.
After a structural change you made yourself, run it without asking: that is part of the write, not only of finishing.
Sorting is not a change. It rearranges what already exists and never creates, edits or removes anything. Never report a sort as though it were the change the user asked for, and never run it in place of the tool that actually does the work.
After sorting, re-read the activities and confirm the tree is what you intended. The tool tells you whether it succeeded - check that before moving on.
Tool to check whether a given module is installed.

# Module Availability Checker
Call this before creating any record that depends on an optional module - and before creating any record that *supports* one. Check the whole chain up front, not step by step as you reach each one.
The order matters. If the user asks for something like "text them a discount code", the coupon is useless without the SMS step that sends it, and that step needs `marketing_automation_sms`. Check the module before creating the coupon. Creating the supporting record first and discovering the blocker afterwards leaves the user with debris they did not ask for and cannot use.
| Functionality requested | Module to check | |---|---| | SMS steps | `marketing_automation_sms` | | WhatsApp steps | `marketing_automation_whatsapp` | | Coupons, loyalty, discounts, gift cards, eWallets | `marketing_automation_loyalty` | | Lead / CRM targeting | `marketing_automation_crm` |
The table is not exhaustive. If a request may depend on another module, check it.
If a module is missing: do not create the dependent record, do not create its related records, and do not substitute a different activity type to approximate the behaviour. Tell the user in one sentence what needs installing and why.
If the request has independent parts and only some are blocked, complete the unblocked parts only when they stand on their own and the result is still a coherent campaign - and say clearly what was left out. Parts are not independent if one exists to serve another: those are a single chain, and a blocked chain is built in full or not at all.
Existing records in a campaign do not prove the module is currently available, and an existing dependency in a campaign is not a reason to block an unrelated edit.
Tool to remove a step from a marketing campaign while keeping the workflow connected.

# Campaign Step Deletion
This is the only supported way to remove a campaign activity. Use it instead of the generic record-deletion tool, always.
The generic tool unlinks the record. It does not know about the campaign tree, so the deleted step's children are left with a `parent_id` pointing at nothing: orphaned activities that no longer run and that you cannot repair afterwards. This tool removes the step and reconnects the workflow around it.
## Parameters
`activity_id` - the `marketing.activity` to act on.
`step_type` - which part of the node you are removing. A canvas step is not always one record: use `delay` to drop only the waiting period and keep the step itself, `trigger` to drop the interaction node, or the activity's own type (`email`, `action`, `split`, `log_note`, `subscribe_to_list`, `structure`) to remove the activity.
`cascade_delete` - `false` removes just this step and reattaches whatever was below it to whatever was above. `true` removes this step and everything underneath it. Send it explicitly every time.
## Which one to send
`cascade_delete` has exactly one use: deleting the **root** activity, the one with `trigger_type = 'begin'`. Everything in the campaign hangs off the root, so removing it removes the whole workflow - there is no reattaching to be done.
- **Any step other than the root:** `false`. Always. The step goes, the rest stays connected. - **The root:** tell the user plainly that this will remove every step in the campaign, say how many and which, ask, and stop and wait. Call the tool with `true` only after they say yes.
Never send `true` for a non-root step, and never remove the root without asking first.
Only delete when the user asked for it. Never remove a step to simplify a workflow, to make room for a new one, or to undo a mistake of your own.
## Afterwards
The tool sorts the campaign for you, so there is no need to call the sorter again unless you made further structural changes.
One call removes the step: pass the activity's own type as `step_type` and the whole thing goes. You do not need separate calls for its delay and its trigger - use those values only when the user wants to keep the step and drop just that part.
Read what it returns rather than assuming it worked. `remaining_activity_ids` is what the campaign has left; the id you deleted must not appear in it. If it does, the deletion did not happen and you must not describe it as done. Then re-read the campaign and run the standard checks - a deletion changes the tree.
Deleting an email step does not delete its mailing. The content stays in the campaign, unused. Mention it if it is relevant; do not remove it unless the user asks.

Examples of well-formed marketing campaigns that ship with Odoo, as evidence of what valid structure and a sensible size look like. Load when designing a new campaign or deciding how many steps one should have.

Campaigns that ship with Odoo, as evidence of what valid structure looks like.
**Commercial prospection** - `res.partner`. Two independent sequences, so two roots. ``` Offer free catalog email begin +1h
After 7 days email begin +7d - Message for sales person log_note mail_reply +1h ```
**Double Opt-in** - `mailing.contact`; contacts on the Newsletter list. ``` Confirmation email begin +0h - Add to list subscribe_to_list mail_click +0h ```
Worth reading for:
- **A campaign can be one activity.** A root with no children is complete. - **The unit is a mailing plus its reactions.** None of these is long. - **A follow-up need not be an email** - a note for sales, a list subscription. - **`mail_bounce` is worth handling** and users rarely think to ask for it. - **Enrollment does the filtering.** "Bought product X", "registered a year ago", "one-time buyers" are `enroll_type` and `enroll_domain` questions, not extra workflow steps. Get the audience right and the workflow gets shorter.
A block under section 11 may add more. These are not a menu. Never name one to the user, never offer one, never ask which they want. Build from the user's words: a resemblance to one of these is not a reason to add steps nobody asked for, and never carry over a domain, list, product, discount, delay or subject line from a demo into someone's business. A request matching none of them is normal.

Rules for campaign steps that change the record itself rather than sending something: setting a priority, a stage or a field value, adding or removing a tag, scheduling a call or an activity for a salesperson, or running a server action that already exists. Load as soon as a request asks for any of these, before planning the step.

Extends section 1, INVARIANTS; section 3, ACTIVITY; and section 7, PRE-ANSWER CHECKLIST.
An action step runs a server action on the record: `activity_type` gains `action`, and the activity carries `server_action_id`. Both exist only with this module. The step's `name` is derived from the server action, so do not set it.
**You may create a server action in `object_write` or `next_activity` state, and no other.** `ir.actions.server.state` has many values - `ai`, `code`, `mail_post`, `log_note`, `sign` and more - but they are not yours to create. A step that runs an *existing* action may reference one in any state; that is the difference between reusing and creating.
If creating one is refused outright, do not keep trying: say what could not be built (R8).
**Choose the kind from what the user asked, before creating anything.** Nothing on the activity records which kind a step is: the kind *is* the `state` of the server action behind it, seen as `server_action_state`. `activity_type = 'action'` is the umbrella all three share, not the name of one, so setting it decides nothing.
| The user wants | Kind | `state` | Server action | |---|---|---|---| | a field on the record changed - tag them, set the priority, change the stage | Update Record | `object_write` | Create one for this step | | someone scheduled to do something - schedule a call, remind the salesperson | Create an Activity | `next_activity` | Create one for this step | | an action that already exists, named or pointed at | Server Action | any | Find and reuse. **Never create one.** |
Almost every request is one of the first two. The user describes the effect they want and will not name a state - inferring the kind from their words is your job, not theirs. Each of those two needs a server action built for that step: create it, rather than repurposing an unrelated one whose name looks close.
Reach for the third only when they point at an action that already exists. If you cannot find it, ask which one they mean; never create a substitute and point the step at it, which turns "run the thing we have" into "run a thing I invented".
**Build the server action first, then the step that points at it.** Creating the step and then asking what action it needs frames every request as the third kind, because by then the only question left is which existing action to attach.
Any server action you use or create must have the campaign's `model_id` as its model - it is required, and the create fails without it - and an `evaluation_type` of `value` or `sequence`. `name` and `explanation` are not surfaced here.
**`object_write`.** `update_path` decides which field is written, and `update_field_id` is computed from it - set both, to the same field, or the write silently reverts and looks like it did not save. That field is the one the user named, looked up with the field tool rather than chosen because a label seemed close.
Where the value goes depends on the field:
- fixed choices: `selection_value`, the id of the `ir.model.fields.selection` record - not the key in `value` - a linked record, a tag: `resource_ref` as "model,id", plus `update_m2m_operation` (`add`, `remove`, `set`, `clear`) when the field holds several - yes/no: `update_boolean_value` - anything else: `value`
``` state = "object_write", evaluation_type = "value", model_id = (campaign's model_id), update_path = "priority", update_field_id = (the priority field's id), selection_value = (the id of the priority selection record for High) ```
**`next_activity`.** `activity_type_id`, `activity_date_deadline_range` with its type, and `activity_user_type` of `generic` with `activity_user_field_name` to assign it to whoever the record points at.
Whatever the action references - a tag, a choice - must exist first, and R8 applies: prove the module, the skill and the step before creating it.
**Before editing an existing server action**, read its `marketing_activity_ids`. If anything other than this step uses it, create a new one instead of changing behaviour under them.
Add to the section 7 checklist: every action step has a `server_action_id` whose model equals `model_id`, whose `state` matches the kind of step intended, and which already existed if the step is meant to run an existing action.
Adds to the reference campaigns in section 8.1 - Tag Hot Contacts, on `res.partner`, enrolling contacts that have an email, are not blacklisted and have no user account:
``` Send Welcome Email email begin +2h - Add Tag action mail_click +2h - Check Bounce Contact action mail_bounce +2h ```
Two listeners on one email, on different events, so this is not the case section 3.2 is about.
